title: "Lorenz Attractor Explorer"
subtitle: "Chaos, sensitive dependence, and the geometry of a strange attractor"
page-layout: full

The Lorenz system
$$x' = \sigma(y-x),\qquad y' = x(\rho - z) - y,\qquad z' = xy - \beta z$$
is a three-dimensional autonomous system whose solutions, for $\sigma = 10$, $\beta = 8/3$, and $\rho = 28$, neither settle to an equilibrium nor to a periodic orbit. Drag the picture to rotate it, slide $\rho$ to watch the behavior change, and use the tabs below the picture to compare two nearby solutions (sensitive dependence), view the time series, and see the Lorenz map of successive maxima of $z$.

Things to try (each link opens the app with those settings):

- [Classic chaos, $\rho = 28$](apps/lorenz.html#s=10&r=28&b=2.666667&tab=sep){target="_blank"}: watch the two solutions, started $10^{-6}$ apart, separate exponentially.
- [Origin attracts, $\rho = 0.5$](apps/lorenz.html#s=10&r=0.5&b=2.666667){target="_blank"} and [spiral into $C_\pm$, $\rho = 15$](apps/lorenz.html#s=10&r=15&b=2.666667){target="_blank"}: the behavior before chaos sets in.
- [Volume contraction](apps/lorenz.html#s=10&r=28&b=2.666667&cloud=1){target="_blank"}: a ball of initial conditions collapses at the rate $e^{-(\sigma+\beta+1)t}$.
- [Lorenz map](apps/lorenz.html#s=10&r=28&b=2.666667&tab=map){target="_blank"}: successive maxima of $z$ lie on a nearly one-dimensional curve.
- [A periodic window, $\rho = 150$](apps/lorenz.html#s=10&r=150&b=2.666667&tab=sep){target="_blank"}: large $\rho$ does not always mean chaos.
